acceptanceCriteria: A command holding the lock beyond the threshold yields a finding naming pid, command and age.
No completions within the window, with ready tickets and idle workers, yields a finding; an empty queue yields none.
Findings clear on their own when the condition ends.
Thresholds are settable, and the defaults are documented.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1041 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Queue slowness has distinct causes that today need hand-written plugins: a process holding the store or preparation lock for a long time (others fail LOCK_TIMEOUT), queue commands running for a minute or more, no completion for many hours, and file-handle exhaustion. Plugins cannot see lock holders. Current workaround A script walks the process list for long-running queue commands, checks which holds the lock file, compares the last completion time with now, and compares the open-file table with its limit. Proposal Native findings QUEUE_LOCK_HELD (holder pid, command, age), SLOW_QUEUE_COMMAND, NO_COMPLETIONS (window configurable, default 2 h while ready tickets exist) and FD_PRESSURE, with configurable thresholds. See beamfall/corvint#1041 for the full text.
title: doctor: built-in findings for queue lock holders, slow queue commands, completion stalls and file-handle pressure (issue #1041)
